topic: Driving Emergencies - Traffic vs Vehicle Emergencies
question: According to the manual, what is the difference between a "traffic emergency" and a "vehicle emergency"?
choice_a: A traffic emergency occurs when two vehicles are about to collide; a vehicle emergency occurs when tires, brakes, or other critical parts fail
choice_b: A traffic emergency involves brake failure; a vehicle emergency involves a collision
choice_c: A traffic emergency occurs only at intersections; a vehicle emergency occurs only on highways
choice_d: There is no difference between the two terms
explanation: The manual states traffic emergencies occur when two vehicles are about to collide, while vehicle emergencies occur when tires, brakes, or other critical parts fail.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17 - Driving Emergencies

question: Why does the manual say that steering away from an obstacle may be safer than braking in an emergency?
choice_a: Because stopping distance is always shorter than steering distance
choice_b: Because you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_c: Because steering never risks losing control of the vehicle
choice_d: Because brakes are less reliable than steering in all vehicles
explanation: The manual notes that stopping is not always the safest action; you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, though top-heavy vehicles may flip over.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: What does the manual recommend to make sure you can make a quick, safe turn in an emergency?
choice_a: Keep one hand on the wheel and one on the gear shift
choice_b: Steer with your knee if needed to free your hands
choice_c: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times, so you're ready for a quick turn
choice_d: Keep your hands off the wheel until an emergency begins
explanation: The manual says the best way to have both hands on the wheel in an emergency is to keep them there all the time, since a firm two-handed grip is needed to turn quickly.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: If you are blocked by traffic on both sides and must move to avoid a collision, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Move left into the opposing lane
choice_b: Stop the vehicle immediately in your lane
choice_c: Sound your horn and continue straight ahead
choice_d: A move to the right may be best, since it won't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane
explanation: The manual states that if blocked on both sides, a move to the right may be best because it avoids forcing anyone into an opposing lane and a possible head-on collision.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: When leaving the road in an emergency, what braking guidance does the manual give?
choice_a: Avoid using the brakes until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake very gently
choice_b: Apply the brakes as hard as possible immediately
choice_c: Never use the brakes once you leave the road
choice_d: Pump the brakes continuously at highway speed
explanation: The manual advises avoiding brakes until speed drops to about 20 mph to avoid skidding on a loose surface, then braking gently.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash (Leaving the Road)

question: What does the manual recommend to help maintain control if you must drive off the road?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel sharply back onto the road immediately
choice_b: Keep one set of wheels on the pavement, if possible
choice_c: Accelerate to regain traction
choice_d: Shift into neutral and coast
explanation: The manual states keeping one set of wheels on the pavement, if possible, helps maintain control while driving off the road.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash (Leaving the Road)

question: According to the manual, how should you return to the road if forced off it before you could stop?
choice_a: Edge back onto the road gradually to avoid overcorrecting
choice_b: Brake hard while turning the wheel back onto the pavement
choice_c: Hold the wheel tightly and turn sharply enough to get back onto the road safely, without edging back gradually
choice_d: Wait for another vehicle to signal it is safe before turning back
explanation: The manual warns that edging back gradually can cause tires to grab unexpectedly and lose control; instead, hold the wheel tightly and turn back sharply in one steer-counter-steer move.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash (Returning to the Road)

topic: How to Stop Quickly and Safely
question: What is the "controlled braking" method of stopping described in the manual?
choice_a: Pumping the brakes rapidly in short bursts
choice_b: Releasing the brakes completely whenever the vehicle begins to slow
choice_c: Applying the parking brake instead of the service brakes
choice_d: Applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
explanation: With controlled braking, the driver applies the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, while keeping steering wheel movements very small.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.2 - How to Stop Quickly and Safely

topic: How to Stop Quickly and Safely
question: With the "stab braking" method, what should a driver do after the wheels lock up?
choice_a: Release the brakes, then reapply them fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_b: Continue pressing the brake pedal as hard as possible
choice_c: Shift into a higher gear immediately
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel sharply while holding the brakes
explanation: In stab braking, the driver releases the brakes when the wheels lock, then reapplies the brakes fully once the wheels start rolling again, which can take up to a second.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.2 - How to Stop Quickly and Safely

topic: How to Stop Quickly and Safely
question: Why does the manual warn drivers not to "jam on the brakes" in an emergency?
choice_a: It can damage the brake pedal mechanism
choice_b: It keeps the wheels locked up, causing a skid and loss of vehicle control
choice_c: It uses too much brake fluid at once
choice_d: It automatically engages the parking brake
explanation: Emergency braking does not mean pushing the brake pedal as hard as possible; doing so keeps the wheels locked and causes a skid, and skidding wheels cannot be controlled.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.2 - How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: According to the manual, most hydraulic brake failures occur for one of what two reasons?
choice_a: Worn tires and low engine oil
choice_b: Faulty transmission and clutch slippage
choice_c: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
choice_d: Low fuel and overheated engine
explanation: The manual lists loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills as the two main causes of hydraulic brake failure.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure

question: What happens to the brake pedal when the hydraulic system loses pressure and won't build up pressure?
choice_a: The pedal becomes unusually stiff
choice_b: The pedal vibrates rapidly
choice_c: The pedal locks in place
choice_d: The brake pedal will feel spongy or go to the floor
explanation: The manual states that when the hydraulic system won't build up pressure, the brake pedal will feel spongy or go to the floor.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure

question: If you experience loss of hydraulic brake pressure, which action does the manual recommend to help slow the vehicle?
choice_a: Downshift into a lower gear to help slow the vehicle
choice_b: Shift into neutral and coast to a stop
choice_c: Turn off the engine while moving
choice_d: Accelerate to reach a runaway ramp faster
explanation: The manual advises downshifting into a lower gear to help slow the vehicle when hydraulic pressure is lost.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure

question: When using the parking (emergency) brake to slow a vehicle after hydraulic brake failure, what must you do at the same time?
choice_a: Shift into reverse gear
choice_b: Press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time, so you can adjust brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking
choice_c: Turn the steering wheel back and forth continuously
choice_d: Disconnect the trailer brakes
explanation: The manual explains the parking brake is separate from the hydraulic system and can be used to slow the vehicle, but the release button or lever must be pressed or pulled simultaneously to adjust pressure and prevent wheel lockup.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure

question: According to the manual, what is a driver's "best hope" for stopping safely after brake failure on a long downgrade?
choice_a: Shifting into neutral and coasting to a stop
choice_b: Turning off the engine
choice_c: An escape ramp
choice_d: Sounding the horn continuously to warn other drivers
explanation: The manual states that once brakes have failed on a downgrade, your best hope is an escape ramp, and signs will tell you about one if available.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure (Brake Failure on Downgrades)

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a sign of tire failure?
choice_a: A sudden increase in fuel economy
choice_b: The engine temperature gauge rising
choice_c: A dashboard warning chime
choice_d: A loud "bang," heavy vibration or thumping, or the steering feeling "heavy"
explanation: The manual lists sound (a loud bang), vibration/thumping, and a "heavy" feel to the steering as signs of tire failure.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure

question: What does the manual instruct a driver to do immediately if a tire fails?
choice_a: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands and stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed
choice_b: Brake hard immediately to stop as quickly as possible
choice_c: Release the steering wheel to let the vehicle correct itself
choice_d: Accelerate briefly to maintain control
explanation: The manual says to hold the steering wheel firmly (since a front tire failure can twist it out of your hand) and stay off the brake, since braking after tire failure could cause loss of control.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure

question: After stopping safely following a suspected tire failure, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Continue driving if the vehicle seems to handle normally
choice_b: Get out and check all the tires, even if the vehicle seems to be handling all right
choice_c: Only check the tire that made noise
choice_d: Wait for a roadside assistance service before inspecting anything
explanation: The manual advises checking all the tires after stopping, even if the vehicle seems to be handling fine, because a dual tire failure may only be noticeable by looking at it.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure

question: How does the Antilock Braking System (ABS) work, according to the manual?
choice_a: It increases brake pressure whenever the vehicle exceeds the speed limit
choice_b: It applies the parking brake automatically during hard stops
choice_c: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and an electronic control unit (ECU) decreases brake pressure to avoid it
choice_d: It shuts off the engine when wheels begin to skid
explanation: The manual explains sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and the ECU then decreases brake pressure to avoid wheel lockup, adjusting pressure to provide maximum braking without lockup danger.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.1 - How Antilock Braking Systems Work

question: How does ABS relate to a vehicle's normal braking system, per the manual?
choice_a: ABS replaces the normal brakes entirely
choice_b: ABS decreases normal braking capability to prevent skids
choice_c: ABS increases normal braking capability at all times
choice_d: ABS is an addition to normal brakes; it does not decrease or increase normal braking capability and only activates when wheels are about to lock up
explanation: The manual states ABS is an addition to your normal brakes, does not decrease or increase your normal braking capability, and only activates when wheels are about to lock up.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: According to the manual, ABS is required by the Department of Transportation on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after which date?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: The manual states truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to have ABS.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.2 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

topic: How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS
question: Where will tractors, trucks, and buses display an ABS malfunction lamp, according to the manual?
choice_a: On the rear bumper only
choice_b: A yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel
choice_c: On the trailer's front corner only
choice_d: There is no lamp; a warning buzzer sounds instead
explanation: The manual states tractors, trucks, and buses will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the instrument panel.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.3 - How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

topic: How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS
question: Where is the yellow ABS malfunction lamp located on trailers, according to the manual?
choice_a: On the instrument panel inside the cab
choice_b: Underneath the trailer near the axle
choice_c: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
choice_d: On the trailer's rear bumper, centered
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.3 - How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: According to the manual, what is the main benefit of ABS during hard braking?
choice_a: It always shortens stopping distance significantly
choice_b: It eliminates the need for a driver to brake carefully
choice_c: It prevents all types of skids, including those from turning or acceleration
choice_d: It helps you avoid wheel lockup and maintain steering control, letting you steer around an obstacle while braking
explanation: The manual states ABS helps you avoid wheel lockup and maintain control; you may or may not stop faster, but you should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.4 - How ABS Helps You

topic: ABS on the Tractor Only or Only on the Trailer
question: According to the manual, if only the tractor has ABS and the trailer begins to swing out, what should you do?
choice_a: Keep an eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so
choice_b: Immediately apply the parking brake
choice_c: Accelerate to straighten out the trailer
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel sharply into the swing
explanation: The manual states that when only the tractor has ABS, you should keep your eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so, if it begins to swing out.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.5 - ABS on the Tractor Only or Only on the Trailer

question: How should a driver brake in a vehicle equipped with ABS, according to the manual?
choice_a: Pump the brakes rapidly at all times
choice_b: Brake the same way as always, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control
choice_c: Always apply maximum brake force regardless of conditions
choice_d: Avoid using the brakes and rely on engine braking instead
explanation: The manual instructs drivers with ABS to brake as they always have, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.6 - Braking with ABS

topic: Braking If ABS Is Not Working
question: If the ABS malfunction lamp indicates the system isn't working, what does the manual say about your brakes?
choice_a: The vehicle has no brakes and must be towed
choice_b: Only the parking brake will function
choice_c: You still have normal brake functions and should drive and brake as you always have
choice_d: The trailer brakes will automatically disengage
explanation: The manual states that without ABS you still have normal brake functions, and you should drive and brake as you always have.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.7 - Braking If ABS Is Not Working

question: Which of the following is a safety reminder about ABS from the manual?
choice_a: ABS allows you to safely follow more closely
choice_b: ABS allows you to safely drive faster in poor conditions
choice_c: ABS will prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_d: ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully
explanation: The manual's safety reminders state ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.8 - Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual's ABS safety reminders, what types of skids will ABS NOT prevent?
choice_a: Skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_b: Skids caused by over braking on a wet road
choice_c: Brake-induced skids on ice
choice_d: Skids caused by locked wheels during hard braking
explanation: The manual notes ABS should prevent brake-induced skids or jackknifes, but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels (power skids) or going too fast in a turn (turning skids).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.18.8 - Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual, a skid can be caused by which of the following?
choice_a: Using a properly adjusted mirror
choice_b: Over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, or driving too fast for conditions
choice_c: Using the correct tire pressure
choice_d: Signaling before a lane change
explanation: The manual lists four causes of skids: over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast for conditions.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.19 - Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, what is by far the most common type of skid?
choice_a: A front-wheel skid caused by worn brake pads
choice_b: A trailer skid caused by uneven cargo
choice_c: One in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
choice_d: A skid caused entirely by underinflated tires
explanation: The manual states the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.19.1 - Drive-wheel Skids

question: What two actions does the manual instruct to correct a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Accelerate and turn away from the skid
choice_b: Apply the parking brake and steer straight
choice_c: Downshift and pump the brakes
choice_d: Stop braking (to let the rear wheels roll again) and counter-steer
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again, and to counter-steer as the vehicle turns back on course.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.19.2 - Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: According to the manual, what is the only way to stop a front-wheel skid?
choice_a: Stop turning and/or braking so hard, and slow down as quickly as possible without skidding
choice_b: Turn the steering wheel more sharply in the direction of the skid
choice_c: Accelerate to regain front tire traction
choice_d: Apply the parking brake immediately
explanation: The manual states that in a front-wheel skid, the only way to stop the skid is to let the vehicle slow down by easing off the turning and/or braking.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.19.3 - Front-wheel Skids

question: What are the basic steps the manual says should be taken at any accident where you are not seriously hurt?
choice_a: Move the vehicles involved back to their original positions, notify a tow truck, and wait
choice_b: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured
choice_c: Take photographs, exchange insurance information, and leave the scene
choice_d: Call your dispatcher first, then protect the area
explanation: The manual lists the basic steps at any accident as: protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.20 - Accident Procedures

question: According to the manual, which of these is a step to protect an accident area?
choice_a: Leave your vehicle exactly where it stopped, even if it's blocking traffic
choice_b: Park as close to the wreckage as possible to shield it
choice_c: Put on your flashers and set out reflective triangles so other drivers can see them in time
choice_d: Wait for police before doing anything
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to put on flashers and set out reflective triangles to warn other traffic, giving them time to avoid the accident.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.20.1 - Protect the Area

question: If you have a cell phone or CB radio at an accident scene, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Wait until the scene is fully cleaned up before calling
choice_b: Only call if someone is seriously injured
choice_c: Ask a passing driver to call instead
choice_d: Call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle, if possible
explanation: The manual states that if you have a cell phone or CB, you should call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.20.2 - Notify Authorities

question: According to the manual, when should you avoid moving a severely injured person at an accident scene?
choice_a: Unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_b: Under no circumstances, ever
choice_c: Only if a doctor is not present
choice_d: Unless they ask to be moved
explanation: The manual instructs not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.20.3 - Care for the Injured

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a possible cause of vehicle fires?
choice_a: Properly inflated tires
choice_b: Short circuits due to damaged insulation or loose electrical connections
choice_c: A fully charged fire extinguisher
choice_d: A well-ventilated cargo area
explanation: The manual lists short circuits due to damaged insulation and loose connections in the electrical system as a cause of vehicle fires.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.21.1 - Causes of Fire

question: According to the manual, what should a vehicle inspection for fire prevention include?
choice_a: Only checking the fuel level
choice_b: Only checking tire tread depth
choice_c: A complete inspection of the electrical, fuel, and exhaust systems, tires, and cargo, and checking that the fire extinguisher is charged
choice_d: Only checking the cargo manifest
explanation: The manual states a complete vehicle inspection for fire prevention should cover the electrical, fuel, and exhaust systems, tires, and cargo, and confirm the fire extinguisher is charged.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.21.2 - Fire Prevention

question: According to the manual, where should you park a vehicle that has caught fire?
choice_a: As close to other vehicles as possible for shared safety
choice_b: Near a service station so help is nearby
choice_c: In the nearest traffic lane with flashers on
choice_d: In an open area, away from buildings, trees, brush, other vehicles, or anything that might catch fire
explanation: The manual instructs parking in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, other vehicles, or anything flammable, and specifically warns not to pull into a service station.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual, why should you keep the doors shut on a cargo fire in a van or box trailer?
choice_a: Opening the doors supplies the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast
choice_b: Opening the doors releases toxic smoke into the cab
choice_c: It is required by hazardous materials placarding rules
choice_d: Opening the doors voids the cargo insurance
explanation: The manual warns that opening the van doors on a cargo fire supplies oxygen and can cause the fire to burn very fast, especially with hazardous materials cargo.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual, where should you aim a fire extinguisher when fighting a fire?
choice_a: Up into the flames, as high as possible
choice_b: At the source or base of the fire, staying as far away as possible
choice_c: At the smoke, not the flames
choice_d: Directly at the fuel tank
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stay as far from the fire as possible and aim the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not up in the flames.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual's fire class chart, which class of fire should NOT be extinguished with water because it can cause shock?
choice_a: Class A - wood, paper, ordinary combustibles
choice_b: Class B - gasoline, oil, grease
choice_c: Class C - electrical equipment fires
choice_d: Class D - combustible metals
explanation: The manual states Class C electrical equipment fires should be extinguished with non-conducting agents like carbon dioxide or dry chemicals, and warns not to use water because it can cause shock.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.21 - Fires (Class/Type of Fires, Figure 2.20)

question: According to the manual, how fast can the liver process alcohol?
choice_a: About one drink every 15 minutes
choice_b: About two drinks per hour
choice_c: Alcohol is processed instantly once it reaches the liver
choice_d: Only about one-third an ounce per hour, a fixed rate that only time, not coffee or a cold shower, can change
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, a fixed rate, so only time (not coffee or a cold shower) will sober a person up.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving

question: According to the manual, what does Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measure?
choice_a: The amount of alcohol in a person's body/blood
choice_b: The number of drinks consumed in the last hour only
choice_c: The driver's reaction time in seconds
choice_d: The percentage of alcohol in a specific beverage
explanation: The manual explains BAC commonly measures the amount of alcohol in your body, recorded in milligrams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving (Figure 2.22)

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a driving error caused by alcohol?
choice_a: Improved night vision
choice_b: Straddling lanes, quick jerky starts, and running stop signs or red lights
choice_c: Faster reaction time to hazards
choice_d: Better judgment about following distance
explanation: The manual lists effects of alcohol on driving including straddling lanes, quick jerky starts, not signaling, and running stop signs and red lights.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving

question: According to the manual, when is possession and use of a drug prescribed by a doctor permitted for a driver?
choice_a: Never, regardless of the doctor's instructions
choice_b: Only if the drug is an over-the-counter cold medicine
choice_c: If the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_d: Only after the driver passes a drug test
explanation: The manual states possession and use of a doctor-prescribed drug is permitted if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.22.2 - Other Drugs

question: According to the manual, what should you do if you become too ill to operate a motor vehicle safely?
choice_a: Continue driving carefully at a reduced speed
choice_b: Drive only on back roads until you feel better
choice_c: Take an over-the-counter medication and continue the trip
choice_d: You must not drive, except in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop
explanation: The manual states that if you become too ill to drive safely, you must not drive, though in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.22.3 - Illness

question: How does the manual define hazardous materials?
choice_a: Products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation
choice_b: Any cargo weighing more than 10,000 pounds
choice_c: Only materials labeled "flammable"
choice_d: Only liquids transported in bulk tanks
explanation: The manual defines hazardous materials as products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.23.1 - What Are Hazardous Materials?

question: According to the manual, the rules about transporting hazardous materials are intended to do which of the following?
choice_a: Reduce delivery costs for shippers
choice_b: Contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment
choice_c: Eliminate the need for shipping papers
choice_d: Allow any driver to transport any hazardous material without an endorsement
explanation: The manual states the intent of hazardous materials rules is to contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.23.2 - Why Are There Rules?

question: According to the manual, what are hazardous materials identification numbers used for, and what precedes them?
choice_a: They are two-digit codes preceded by "HM" used only by shippers
choice_b: They are used only for cargo tanks and preceded by "TX"
choice_c: They are four-digit codes, preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN," used by first responders to identify hazardous materials
choice_d: They are barcodes scanned only at weigh stations
explanation: The manual states identification numbers are a four-digit code used by first responders to identify hazardous materials, preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN."
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.23.3 - Lists of Regulated Products

question: According to the manual, how many identical placards must a placarded vehicle display, and where?
choice_a: Two placards, on the front and rear only
choice_b: One placard, centered on the trailer
choice_c: Three placards, on the rear and both sides
choice_d: At least four identical placards, on the front, rear, and both sides
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides, readable from all four directions.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.23.3 - Lists of Regulated Products

question: According to the manual, a tank endorsement is required for a commercial vehicle designed to transport liquid or gaseous materials in a tank with what minimum capacities?
choice_a: An individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_b: Any tank capacity, regardless of size
choice_c: An individual rated capacity of more than 500 gallons only
choice_d: An aggregate capacity of 5,000 gallons or more only
explanation: The manual states a tank endorsement is required for a vehicle with a tank of individual rated capacity more than 119 gallons and aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, whether or not the liquid or gas is hazardous.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 2.23.3 - Lists of Regulated Products
